sections.heading: 1. Turn switching intent into a completed migration
paragraphs: The competitor_intent_comparison_hijacking play captures an existing buying decision without pretending to be the incumbent. Build separate pages for [Legacy SaaS] pricing, cancel, alternative, and export searches only when each page answers a distinct operational question. A pricing visitor needs dated seat limits and a total ownership calculation. An export visitor needs a working sample file and a field map. A cancellation visitor needs accurate instructions and a clear distinction between leaving the old service and purchasing yours. Start with three competitors whose exports you can actually parse, not hundreds of generated doorway pages. Track qualified sessions through successful import, first useful output, and paid activation. Model 10-18% conversion from completed, qualified importer sessions to paid accounts within thirty days; never present that denominator as all search traffic.

Offer a one-click CSV migration importer after the customer selects their own export. Validate required columns, encoding, dates, duplicate identifiers, and attachment references before committing records. Show accepted rows and rejected rows separately, preserve an import receipt, and make retries idempotent. A free micro-tool can scan a small sample for broken references without retaining the original file indefinitely. Keep deterministic parsing outside the model; use inference only for ambiguous labels with a bounded review queue. The paid event is a usable reconciliation, not a file upload. Measure cost per successful migration including failed attempts, storage, support minutes, and abuse. Set file size and free credit limits so a popular comparison page cannot spend tomorrow's subscription receipts tonight. Keep the scanner useful even when the visitor never buys.

Make the interactive ROI calculator editable rather than theatrical. Ask for seats, monthly jobs, current invoices, review minutes, and an explicit hourly labor assumption. Display subscription fees, migration effort, inference overages, and remaining human review on both sides. Time saved is capacity released, not automatically payroll eliminated. Date competitor prices and link the relevant public plan descriptions; distinguish verified limits from customer supplied assumptions. Use incumbent names only to identify the products being compared, with no borrowed trade dress or implied sponsorship. Section 1125(c)(3)(A) addresses fair use exclusions from trademark dilution, including identifying and comparing goods; it is not blanket immunity from confusion claims. Review headlines and import labels against that distinction. Archive calculator versions so a prospect can reproduce the numbers that influenced their purchase decision.

sections.heading: 2. Make the customer workflow distribute the product
paragraphs: The viral_distribution_loops play begins with a report the customer already needs to send. For a vertical reconciliation product, ship an embeddable status widget, a downloadable client report, and a small attribution link to the free scanner. Model each customer workflow exposing 5-20 external peers, but distinguish total deliveries from unique recipients and recipients from qualified prospects. Ten reports delivered to the same accountant do not create ten prospects. Record aggregate referral events without leaking invoice contents into analytics. Public widgets should contain only customer selected summaries, with revocable links and private details behind account access. Let paying users remove branding where the plan permits it. Forced promotion damages the report's utility and can turn an otherwise durable distribution mechanism into a reason to cancel the subscription entirely.

Treat the loop as a measured funnel rather than a viral coefficient invented in a spreadsheet. Suppose 100 monthly workflows each reach ten unique peers before overlap, producing 1,000 gross exposures. After deduplication, perhaps 600 people remain; a hypothetical 5% click rate creates thirty visits, and three paid activations represent a useful but modest contribution. Those numbers are assumptions for instrument design, not evidence of demand. Attribute conversions to the originating report with a short lived referral identifier, then compare retained gross profit against widget maintenance and support. Avoid paying for raw shares, which encourages irrelevant distribution. If you reward referrals or feature compensated customer endorsements, disclose the material relationship clearly alongside the recommendation. The FTC endorsement guides address this issue; an unexplained badge is not a substitute for a meaningful disclosure.

The youtube_faceless_high_cpc_compilation_arbitrage play should compile original screen recordings into exact problem walkthroughs, not recycle other creators' footage. Target searches such as an expired API token, a rejected invoice schema, or a failed compliance report export. Show the error, reproduce it with synthetic records, apply the fix, and verify the resulting output. Remove credentials and real customer data before recording. Explain any relevant reporting limitation rather than suggesting that a successful API response proves legal compliance. Link the matching free scanner with a tagged URL and a version dated transcript. Measure tutorial assisted activation and support reduction, not advertising revenue implied by expensive keywords. Refresh videos when APIs change; an obsolete fix creates tickets. Batch four focused tutorials monthly only after their underlying fixes work reliably in the product.

sections.heading: 3. Automate answers without automating expensive mistakes
paragraphs: Build automated AI documentation from versioned product behavior, not an unrestricted crawl of miscellaneous advice. Each answer should retrieve the relevant plan, integration version, and error code before generating an explanation. Link the underlying documentation and expose the exact next action. Cache common explanations and use templates for deterministic failures such as missing columns or expired tokens. Route account access disputes, ambiguous accounting treatments, and unsupported integration behavior to a human with the diagnostic bundle attached. Do not let a support answer silently mutate customer records or issue refunds. The goal is to remove repetitive diagnosis while preserving reliable resolution. Measure verified ticket deflection as sessions that resolve a task without reopening within seven days, not sessions where a chat window merely disappears. Audit a sample of apparently successful sessions weekly.

Meter the engine at the job level. Store model cost, retries, retrieval cost, elapsed time, and whether the output passed deterministic checks. A cheaper answer that generates a second ticket can be more expensive than a larger model answering once. Use a narrow response schema for field suggestions and reject malformed outputs before they reach the importer. Protect tenant boundaries in retrieval and treat uploaded instructions as data rather than authority over the assistant. Set spending limits by account and reserve enough capacity for paid workflows when free scanner demand spikes. Keep a degraded mode that still validates files and serves static documentation during inference outages. This architecture turns availability into a product property instead of a promise that the upstream model provider will never fail during a customer's deadline.

Assign the one full-time owner to product decisions, sales diagnosis, and exception handling. Give one contractor integration maintenance and the other documentation, tutorial production, and support coverage under explicit monthly budgets. Contractor availability is not equivalent to two full-time employees; specify purchased hours and response windows. Review the twenty most frequent failure signatures every Monday and choose one fix that removes future work. If an integration change creates fifty identical tickets, repair the parser and publish a versioned answer before expanding the support queue. Tie documentation changes to product releases so screenshots, API examples, and generated answers remain aligned. Keep a human reachable for unresolved cases, with an honest expected response time. Automation earns its place through lower cost per resolved customer job, not through the percentage of conversations it monopolizes.

sections.heading: 4. Recover failed renewals and separate retention denominators
paragraphs: Begin payment recovery before expiration when the processor provides reliable card metadata: send a practical update reminder fourteen days before expiry and another three days before it. Account updater services may refresh credentials without customer action, so suppress stale reminders after an update. After a failed renewal, classify the decline rather than retrying every card on the same schedule. A temporary funding failure may justify processor scheduled retries; a stolen card or revoked authorization needs a new payment method, not repeated attempts. Send a secure hosted update link to the billing contact immediately, then follow up around days three and seven while respecting processor and network restrictions. Describe the invoice, service impact, and recovery path plainly. Keep promotional offers out of these operational messages so their purpose remains account maintenance.

Use 45-65% recovery of initially failed B2B card renewal invoices within thirty days as a testable planning range, not a universal benchmark or a causal claim about your emails. Count each invoice once, including those recovered by updater services or processor retries, and report incremental lift separately if a suitable comparison cohort exists. On $2,000 of initially failed renewals, that range implies $900-$1,300 collected and $1,100-$700 still unresolved before later collections. Subtract refunds, processor charges, and support effort when estimating economic benefit. Recovery is collection of existing revenue, not new ARR to add a second time. Track both invoice count and dollar recovery because one large account can distort the result. Stop sequences after payment, cancellation, or a payment dispute, and make webhook processing idempotent to prevent duplicate notices.

The base illustration assumes 2.8% net monthly logo churn, defined here as cancellations less reactivated accounts divided by opening customers, excluding new acquisitions. At 210 opening customers that is 5.88 net lost logos in expectation, so roughly six new accounts are needed monthly just to maintain the customer base. Seat and credit expansion cannot replace those logos; it can offset their approximately $876.12 of lost list-price MRR. Show expansion, contraction, reactivation, and new sales separately in the revenue bridge. Avoid confusing net revenue retention with net logo retention. Classify commercial nurture separately from transactional billing notices under section 7704 and applicable primary-purpose rules. Commercial messages need accurate headers, required identification and address information, and a working opt-out honored within the statutory period. Do not turn dunning into disguised acquisition mail.

sections.heading: 5. Reconcile the $375,000 base case dollar by dollar
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative vertical B2B product that reconciles agency client billing exports and drafts exception reports. Its 210 customers pay a $149 monthly list price, generating $31,290 before recurring concessions. Subtract $40 of monthly account credits to reach exactly $31,250 MRR and $375,000 ARR. Consequently, realized ARPU is approximately $148.81; describing $149 as exact realized ARPU would conceal the reconciliation. ARR is a snapshot annualization, not proof that the business collected that amount during its first year. The annual profit illustration assumes this revenue level persists for twelve months, with expansion and acquisition maintaining the base. Gross subscription billings here exclude sales taxes collected for remittance and exclude one-time migration fees. Keep recognized revenue and collected cash schedules separately when annual prepayments or failed renewals cause them to differ from recurring billings.

Deduct $3,100 monthly inference and infrastructure COGS, leaving $28,150 of contribution before the other operating costs shown below. That subtotal is not owner profit and is not a fully loaded gross margin if delivery labor sits elsewhere. The remaining $18,775 monthly cost budget produces $9,375 owner profit, or $112,500 annually. The owner is the single full-time operator; the two contractors share an $8,000 monthly services budget. Additional support coverage and specialist maintenance are purchased from vendors, not silently counted as extra full-time staff. Owner profit is before personal income taxes and includes compensation for the owner's work because no separate owner salary is deducted. A buyer hiring a replacement operator must subtract that salary and employment costs. Treat this as an operating model, not a documented customer success story or a valuation forecast.

Stress the model before calling it high margin. Conservative annual gross billings of $50,000 at 15% leave $7,500 net with 1 FT + 2 C; this cannot fund ordinary full-time owner compensation, so contractor scopes must be small and the owner needs other runway. Base annual gross billings of $375,000 at 30% leave $112,500 net with the same pod, using the explicit expense ledger. Scaled annual gross billings of $700,000 at 45% leave $315,000 net with 2 FT + 3 C only if the $385,000 total cost envelope pays the additional employee, contractors, infrastructure, and acquisition. These margins are assumptions, not automatic economies of scale. If base inference costs double without higher prices, annual owner profit falls by $37,200 to $75,300. If acquisition stalls, expansion may protect revenue temporarily while customer concentration worsens.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you scale a small SaaS pod and prepare a transferable acquisition asset?
chapters.title: Small-Team Scaling, Micro-Extension Rollups & 4x-6x ARR Exit Readiness
chapters.subtitle: The 1 FT + 2 Contractor SaaS Pod, Buying Distribution via Dormant Extensions, Authority SERP Seeding & Clean Micro-PE Exit Diligence
chapters.executive_summary: Scale the workflow before the payroll. A technical founder, an evaluation engineer, and a growth specialist can operate a narrow subscription product when tenant costs, support ownership, and release recovery are explicit. Buy neglected distribution only after verifying active users and transferable rights. Build authority through useful, disclosed participation rather than rented identities. Treat an exit multiple as a negotiation assumption, not cash already earned. This chapter connects staffing, acquisition economics, incident discipline, and buyer evidence while separating recurring billings, delivery costs, operating expenses, and the owner's actual residual profit.

sections.heading: 1. Give the three-person pod explicit ownership
paragraphs: Start with 1 FT Technical/Product Founder + 2 Contractors: Full-Stack/Eval Engineer and Growth/Customer-Success Specialist. The founder owns product scope, pricing, cash, architecture, and incident command. The engineer owns integrations, regression evaluations, release packaging, and restoration drills. The growth specialist owns activation, renewals, customer interviews, and documented acquisition experiments. Contractors are scheduled capacity, not imaginary employees available continuously. Write weekly hours, response windows, substitution rights, and handoff expectations into the operating calendar. Give every production system a primary owner and a named backup, with individual access rather than shared passwords. Reserve founder time for the work only the founder can do: choosing the customer problem and refusing expensive exceptions. A pod fails when every question travels through one person, even if the payroll looks impressively small on paper.

Run Monday as a thirty minute allocation meeting using the previous week's customer and cost evidence. Select one activation improvement, one reliability repair, and one distribution test; assign an owner and a measurable finish condition to each. Tuesday and Wednesday carry implementation and customer observation. Thursday is the release window, with evaluation results attached and a tested rollback available. Friday closes the billing reconciliation, renewal queue, and support review. Keep urgent incident handling separate from this planned cadence so an outage does not silently erase commitments. At $700k ARR, expand to 2 FT + 3 C only when recurring workload supports the economics: add a full-time operations or engineering lead and a third contractor for integrations or specialist support. Preserve explicit ownership rather than creating five interchangeable generalists.

The scenario labels describe annual gross subscription billings, not cash the owner can withdraw immediately. Conservative means $50,000 gross and a 15% residual margin, or $7,500 net; Base means $375,000 and 30%, or $112,500 net; Scaled means $700,000 and 45%, or $315,000 net. Define this residual consistently as pretax operating owner profit after delivery costs, contractor invoices, and a recorded founder compensation allowance. Personal taxes, acquisition financing, and sale proceeds sit outside it. The conservative case cannot fund a market-rate full-time founder and two substantial contractor retainers from revenue alone. It therefore requires limited contractor hours, a low founder allowance, or separate runway. Show any underpayment explicitly, because a buyer will normalize replacement labor and may reduce the profit figure used to price the business.

table.caption: Forensic operating traps
rows: Scheduled backup and reduced service scope

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile recurring revenue and delivery cost weekly
paragraphs: Maintain a weekly SaaS scorecard with New MRR, Expansion MRR, Churned MRR, Net MRR, Gross Margin >= 82%, and Token Cost / Tenant. Define New MRR as newly activated paying subscriptions at normalized monthly prices, excluding trials and implementation fees. Expansion MRR measures increases from existing customers; record contractions separately so downgrades cannot disappear. Churned MRR records recurring revenue lost through cancellations. Define Net MRR change as new plus expansion plus reactivation minus contraction minus churn, then reconcile opening MRR plus that change to closing MRR. Keep annual prepayments divided by twelve in the recurring ledger while retaining their actual cash receipt dates elsewhere. Label discounts, refunds, delinquent subscriptions, and foreign exchange effects explicitly. A dashboard number that cannot reconcile to subscription events is decoration, not acquisition evidence.

Calculate gross margin from recognized subscription revenue less delivery COGS, divided by that revenue. Include inference, hosting, storage, usage-linked vendors, payment processing, and directly attributable service labor under a consistent accounting policy. Track research and product development separately as operating expense; do not improve margin by moving recurring customer support out of delivery costs without explanation. At an illustrative $700,000 annual revenue run rate, an 82% gross margin allows $126,000 of delivery costs and leaves $574,000 gross profit. Reaching $315,000 residual owner profit then allows $259,000 for remaining operating expenses, including the stated compensation allowance. The arithmetic is a budget, not proof that five people's labor fits. Price the actual hours and retainers first, then revise scope or pricing if the staffing model exceeds the envelope.

Token Cost / Tenant should show median, ninety-fifth percentile, and maximum monthly inference spend alongside requests, retries, and paid plan. Averages hide one customer whose automated imports consume the month's contribution. Instrument model calls with tenant identifiers, model version, input size, output size, cache outcome, and vendor invoice reconciliation. Avoid storing sensitive prompt contents merely to allocate cost. Establish per-plan usage budgets, bounded retries, queued batch work, and a cheaper evaluated route for routine tasks. Recalculate the entire scorecard at unsubsidized vendor prices before expanding commitments. A credit balance reaching zero next quarter is a scheduled expense increase, not a surprise incident. Review high-cost tenants with the growth specialist so packaging changes reflect customer value instead of imposing arbitrary limits that trigger avoidable cancellations and support work.

sections.heading: 3. Buy distribution assets, not inflated installation counts
paragraphs: The expired_chrome_extension_acquisitions play targets neglected Chrome extensions or Jira/Shopify plugins with 10k-250k reported users. Treat the label as a sourcing category, not permission to seize abandoned accounts. Negotiate with the verified owner, inspect platform transfer rules, and validate active usage before discussing price. An illustrative offer at 1-2x annual cashflow must use normalized trailing cashflow after maintenance and support, not seller screenshots or gross revenue. Inspect source dependencies, permission scope, reviews, refunds, and whether a working product remains available. Cross-sell a genuinely adjacent AI SaaS feature through transparent product messaging without silently expanding access to customer data. The attraction is existing customer attention, but an installed base is neither a transferable mailing list nor evidence that customers want your subscription. Test that proposition before paying for scale.

Calling this $0 CAC means zero incremental paid-media spend, not zero economic acquisition cost. Suppose a plugin earns $12,000 normalized annual cashflow and costs $18,000 to buy, with $6,000 of integration work. If 120 genuinely incremental SaaS customers activate, the upfront acquisition and integration allocation is $200 per customer before ongoing support and outreach labor. Measure contribution payback using their actual retention and gross profit, not their first invoice alone. Separate the acquired plugin's existing profit from incremental subscription profit so the same dollar does not repay the purchase twice. A small trial placement can reveal conversion without forcing a complete migration. Reject a seller who cannot establish ownership, provide credible usage evidence, or transfer the necessary assets through the platform's documented process. Cheap distribution can otherwise become expensive remediation.

Use reddit_quora_aged_thread_injection as a research label for legitimate evergreen participation, not covert promotion. Find Google Top-3 Reddit, StackOverflow, Quora, or forum threads that match a real customer problem; rankings change, so record the query and observation date. Add a complete answer with reproducible steps and disclose a relevant affiliation where linking is permitted. Do not revive irrelevant discussions, impersonate customers, purchase votes, or turn technical support into repeated advertisements. The platform_privilege_tier_account_arbitrage play should likewise mean earned authority: authentic G2 reviews, a truthful Product Hunt launch, useful GitHub repositories, and maintained ecosystem listings. Never assume purchased reputation or a transferred privileged account survives platform review. Track qualified visits, activated tenants, retained contribution, and time spent; authority only matters commercially when the resulting customers stay and pay.

callout.title: Buy only what can survive transfer
callout.body: A large install count does not repair missing ownership or negative contribution.

Reconcile active users and normalized cashflow.

sections.heading: 4. Keep distribution experiments recoverable and incidents bounded
paragraphs: The ctv_mfa_programmatic_supply_arbitrage mapping is an optional experiment in repurposing B2B dashboard or ambient utility feeds, not a mandate to manufacture ad impressions. Start with an owned, useful display surface such as a public operations feed, with customer data removed and publisher rights documented. CTV inventory is not created merely by putting a dashboard on a television; distribution and ad demand require an eligible platform and accurate inventory declarations. Treat MFA as a warning about low-value made-for-advertising supply rather than a growth target. Never autoplay hidden ads, fabricate viewers, mislabel placements, or resell inventory without authority. Keep any sponsorship or advertising revenue outside SaaS ARR. Measure net contribution after content maintenance, serving costs, revenue share, and invalid-traffic deductions before assigning scarce engineering time to expansion.

Each distribution experiment needs a rollback owner and a ceiling on cash, hours, and customer exposure. Release an acquired extension integration to a small authorized cohort, preserve the existing utility, and watch errors, uninstall rate, permissions complaints, and support volume. A useful incident runbook names the trigger, commander, containment action, customer update owner, recovery check, and evidence location. For runaway inference, stop the affected queue, enforce tenant limits, preserve job identifiers, and reconcile vendor charges. For a model regression, revert the version or route to a tested alternative rather than asking customers to tolerate incorrect output. For a suspected data exposure, isolate affected access, preserve relevant logs, and assess notification duties with qualified support. Do not erase evidence in the rush to make the status page look healthy again.

Practice these runbooks during ordinary working hours before promising response times the pod cannot staff. The founder commands the first incident while the engineer restores service and the growth specialist communicates scope, impact, and the next update time. Avoid publishing a resolution estimate without evidence. Recovery requires a passing customer workflow, queue reconciliation, and checks for duplicated billing or repeated actions, not merely a green process monitor. Record the timeline and assign one preventive change with a date. As the team grows, the second full-time person becomes incident backup so the founder can leave without leaving the business unattended. Map these habits to transferable evidence: dated restoration tests, access inventories, release history, and concise operating notes. Buyers discount systems that depend on undocumented personal memory even when current customers appear satisfied.

sop_steps.detail: Capture tenant scope, errors, spend, and timestamps.

sections.heading: 5. Build a buyer-verifiable earnings and transfer package
paragraphs: A $315k/yr net micro-SaaS does not mechanically produce a $1.5M-$3.5M cash exit. The headline 4x-6x ARR range is an illustrative negotiating assumption, not a verified market comparable or an earnings multiple. Applied to $700,000 ARR, it produces $2.8M-$4.2M enterprise value. A $1.5M-$3.5M enterprise valuation instead represents approximately 2.14x-5x that ARR; cash received at closing can be lower still. Build an explicit proceeds bridge from enterprise value through debt, cash adjustments, working capital, fees, escrow, deferred consideration, and seller financing. For example, a $2.8M enterprise price less $200,000 debt, $100,000 fees, and $300,000 escrow yields $2.2M at closing before tax, assuming no other adjustments. An earnout is contingent consideration, not cash already sold. State every assumption before presenting an exit number to yourself or a buyer.

The Exit-Readiness Diligence Table should connect each assertion to a reproducible file, not a polished pitch. Export a clean Stripe MRR ledger tied to invoices, refunds, bank receipts, and subscription history; document why recognized revenue differs from billings and cash. Demonstrate zero expired-credit cliff by recalculating margins with all promotional infrastructure credits removed and renewals repriced. Target less than 3% monthly churn while specifying whether the figure measures logos or recurring revenue and showing cohort history. Even 3% monthly logo churn compounds to roughly 31% annual loss without replacement, so the threshold alone does not establish durable retention. Separate concentrated customers and acquired cohorts from organic customers. A buyer needs to see whether observed retention survives renewal, a pricing change, and the founder stepping away from daily relationship management.

Prepare a transferable repo, DPA, and IP package before inviting bids. Include signed contractor assignments, dependency licenses, customer contracts, data-processing agreements, domain ownership, and the platform-specific transfer procedure. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), copyright ownership transfers generally require a signed writing; paying an invoice alone is not the same evidence. Review DPA and customer-contract assignment provisions rather than assuming everything moves automatically. Section 1202 of the Internal Revenue Code concerns qualifying small-business stock, with C-corporation, original-issuance, holding-period, asset, and business requirements; an LLC membership sale does not automatically receive that treatment. Acquisition dates and statutory changes matter, so model the actual entity history with a tax adviser. Finally, 15 U.S.C. section 45 makes truthful commercial claims central: invented reviews, inflated users, and misleading savings claims weaken both distribution quality and buyer trust.

chapters.question_prompt: How do I reach ten paying B2B logos in thirty days without building ahead of demand?
chapters.title: The First 30 Days: From Pain Signal to First 10 Paying B2B Logos
chapters.subtitle: Day-by-Day Buyer Discovery, Metered Multi-Tenant MVP Build, Diagnostic-Scanner Outbound & Kill/Pivot/Scale MRR Gates
chapters.executive_summary: Volume 004 scores 88/100 and ranks #02 because narrow business workflows can support recurring revenue, not because models make distribution free. Spend thirty days proving one paid outcome. Interview fifteen buyers, collect three pilot payments before backend work, and build tenant isolation and usage limits before adding acquisition volume. Aim for ten paying business accounts, but let measured activation, contribution margin, and repeat use decide the next investment. This roadmap separates subscription billings from service costs and owner profit, treats scanner results as evidence rather than verdicts, and makes weak demand a reason to stop spending.

key_metrics.label: First value
key_metrics.note: Measure from setup start to useful result

sections.heading: Days 1-7: Sell the narrow outcome before building
paragraphs: Day 1 chooses one buyer, one recurring task, and one measurable failure: for example, agencies checking client sites before monthly reporting. Define the payer separately from the daily user. Day 2 builds a list of forty relevant firms using public technographic signals and manually reviewed G2 one-star complaints. Record the incumbent, complaint date, workflow, estimated frequency, and evidence URL. A complaint is a discovery lead, not proof that a firm wants your product. Avoid copying review text into sales claims or treating an old review as current dissatisfaction. Rank prospects by repeated labor and budget ownership rather than anger. End the day with fifteen scheduled conversations and a falsifiable proposition: this buyer will pay to remove this specific repeated step each month.

Days 3 and 4 run eight and seven structured interviews respectively. Ask buyers to describe their last completed task, show a sanitized input, name the person who approved the incumbent purchase, and quantify time spent checking the output. Ask what happens when the task fails and which existing budget could fund a replacement. Do not ask whether artificial intelligence sounds useful. Capture the same fields for all fifteen interviews so enthusiasm cannot overwhelm contradictory evidence. Count repeated pain only when a recent example supports it. Separate mandatory integration requirements from wishes. Finish each call by offering a paid, bounded pilot with a concrete delivery date, a monthly price, included usage, and an explicit cancellation path. Record objections verbatim in your working notes.

Day 5 turns the strongest repeated problem into a clickable prototype and one diagnostic scan sample built from an authorized example. Show the input, flagged finding, human verification step, and final export; hide no manual work behind a pretend automation. Day 6 demonstrates that sample to qualified buyers and offers a $99-$299 monthly pilot with a stated service start and refund terms if delivery fails. Day 7 requires at least three collected pilot payments or signed paid commitments with enforceable billing dates before backend construction; distinguish unpaid commitments from paying logos. Prefer collected payments. If fewer than three buyers commit, revise the buyer or outcome and repeat discovery. Do not spend the next week building infrastructure to rescue an offer nobody purchased.

table.caption: Forensic checks before more engineering

sections.heading: Days 8-14: Build a bounded tenant, not a general assistant
paragraphs: Day 8 implements a Postgres schema with tenant identifiers on every customer-owned row and row-level security policies tied to authenticated membership. Apply both read predicates and write checks. Never trust a tenant identifier supplied in a request body. Use an application role that cannot bypass RLS; isolate privileged maintenance credentials from request handling. Day 9 tests cross-tenant reads, writes, exports, background jobs, and object storage paths using two deliberately similar accounts. A passing browser test alone proves little if workers run with database ownership privileges. Include connection-pool reuse in the tests so session context cannot leak between requests. Store secrets outside customer records, and make every job carry a validated tenant identity. Reject missing identity rather than guessing a default customer account.

Day 10 installs a zero-data-retention LLM router only on provider endpoints whose contractual terms and technical eligibility actually support ZDR. Do not present a routing flag as a retention guarantee. If no eligible route exists, stop that workload rather than silently forwarding sensitive content elsewhere. Day 11 adds per-tenant token caps, concurrency limits, timeout budgets, and a semantic cache partitioned by tenant, permissions, model, and prompt version. Restrict fuzzy reuse to outputs where near matches cannot alter business facts; use exact keys for account-specific calculations. Reserve estimated credits atomically before a request, then reconcile actual usage after completion. Include retries, embeddings, failed calls, and cache storage in the cost ledger. Prevent duplicate job delivery from charging or executing the same request twice.

Day 12 connects Stripe checkout to a hybrid seat-plus-credit offer: for example, $199 monthly for two seats and a bounded credit allowance. Explain credit units, expiry, overage behavior, and cancellation before purchase. A browser redirect does not establish an entitlement; verified, idempotently processed payment events do. Day 13 builds a golden-eval smoke suite from twenty sanitized examples covering acceptable outputs, required refusals of unsupported claims, prompt injection, and tenant isolation. Keep deterministic security assertions separate from subjective quality scoring. Day 14 reruns the suite against every allowed model route and rehearses a payment failure, exhausted balance, and upstream outage. Permit pilot onboarding only when isolation tests pass, duplicate events are harmless, and the product returns a useful bounded failure instead of an invented answer.

sections.heading: Days 15-21: Convert a verified finding into recurring use
paragraphs: Day 15 onboards the first pilot personally while recording elapsed time from setup start to the first useful export. The target is under five minutes, including connection and configuration time, not merely model latency. Seed a sample workspace when customer access is delayed, but report sample activation separately from live activation. Day 16 removes the largest observed obstacle and adds a concise recovery path for failed imports. Track how many accounts finish without founder intervention and how many return to perform a second real task. With only three pilots, report counts alongside percentages because one customer can swing the rate dramatically. Ask each buyer which output they actually used in their business; a generated report sitting unopened in a workspace is not evidence of delivered value.

Day 17 configures an automated WCAG and technographic scanner for public pages with conservative rate limits, bounded page counts, and no authentication bypass. Respect access restrictions and do not scan private systems without authorization. Automated accessibility checks reveal some detectable issues; they cannot certify complete WCAG conformance or establish legal liability. Day 18 manually verifies the first twenty scan samples before sending any outreach. Use a concrete, reproducible finding, a screenshot where appropriate, and an invitation to inspect the evidence. Commercial email needs accurate headers and subjects, required advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out process under applicable CAN-SPAM rules. Apply suppression immediately operationally and within the statutory deadline. Do not infer that a business address creates a blanket exemption from these requirements.

Day 19 publishes an [Incumbent] alternative comparison calculator with dated public pricing, explicit assumptions, and editable seat and workload inputs. Compare equivalent deliverables; include switching effort rather than declaring your cheaper plan universally superior. Day 20 ships a companion Chrome extension through an appropriate controlled pilot distribution route, with store publication timing tracked separately. Request only permissions needed for the user's explicit page capture, keep credentials server-side, and avoid background collection of browsing history. The extension should shorten the existing task, not become a second product requiring its own roadmap. Day 21 reviews the entire funnel: contacted firms, delivered messages, replies, booked demonstrations, paid logos, live activations, and second uses. Increase outreach only when useful activation accompanies purchases; otherwise fix the first broken transition before importing another prospect list.

sections.heading: Days 22-30 (Phase A — Days 22-28): Reconcile margin and make trust claims inspectable
paragraphs: Day 22 reconciles every tenant's metered requests against provider invoices and hosting allocations. Separate gross subscription billings, recognized revenue, taxes collected, refunds, inference and hosting COGS, payment fees, acquisition expense, support labor, and net owner profit. Do not label the difference between subscriptions and tokens as net profit. For an illustrative $199 monthly tenant, assume $18 inference, $7 allocated hosting, $6 payment fees, and $20 variable support. Service gross margin before payment fees and support is $174, or 87.4%; contribution after those additional variable expenses is $148, or 74.4%. Fixed labor, tools, acquisition, and taxes still remain. Day 23 inspects the worst tenant rather than the average and sets a hard cost ceiling for retries, long contexts, and oversized imports before additional sales expand the loss.

Day 24 activates smart dunning with bounded retries, clear failed-payment messages, a self-service payment update path, and a stated service suspension schedule. Never erase customer work merely because a card retry fails. Keep delinquent balances distinct from collected subscription revenue. Day 25 publishes a trust page describing actual controls, subprocessors, retention settings, deletion handling, and a usable DPA process. State SOC 2 status precisely: no examination, examination underway, or an issued report with its period and scope. A purchased template is not an audit report. Covered online consumer negative-option transactions implicate 15 U.S.C. section 8403; do not claim that provision automatically governs every B2B contract. Transparent recurring prices and easy cancellation remain sound product choices independent of that scope distinction, especially when a pilot converts into an ongoing subscription.

Day 26 reviews customer locations and sales-tax exposure with qualified tax support. Wayfair rejected the physical-presence restriction on nexus; it did not make every SaaS subscription taxable everywhere or create one national threshold. Track state-specific taxability, sourcing, nexus, and registration obligations, and exclude collected sales tax from operating revenue. Day 27 models annual outcomes, not first-month promises: Conservative means $50,000 gross subscription billings and 15% net owner profit, or $7,500, with 1 FT plus 2 C; Base means $375,000 and 30%, or $112,500, with 1 FT plus 2 C; Scaled means $700,000 and 45%, or $315,000, with 2 FT plus 3 C. FT denotes full-time roles and C scoped contractors, not full-time equivalents. Day 28 documents whether founder labor is paid; unpaid founder effort makes the conservative case economically fragile.

sections.heading: Days 29-30: Choose Kill, Fix, or Scale from collected evidence
paragraphs: Day 29 freezes the measurement window and prepares one account-level ledger. Define a paying logo as a distinct external business with a successfully collected recurring subscription and no full refund; multiple seats do not create multiple logos. Define collected MRR as the monthly recurring value represented by paid active subscriptions, normalizing annual contracts and excluding taxes, setup fees, one-time credit purchases, and unpaid invoices. Ten logos at $199 produce $1,990 MRR, not $19,900 and not owner profit. Record the denominator and observation window for activation and repeat use. Count repeat use only for accounts old enough to have completed a seven-day observation period. New accounts remain pending rather than being called retained. Reconcile cost records to the same service period and disclose missing invoices or provisional hosting allocations before interpreting contribution margins.

Day 30 applies ordered rules agreed before the results arrived. Kill the current offer if fewer than three paying logos remain after fifteen completed interviews and thirty qualified offers, or if no eligible pilot repeats the core task within seven days. If that outreach minimum was missed, classify the result as Fix distribution rather than proof of absent demand. Scale only with at least ten paying logos, at least $1,490 collected MRR, eight of the latest ten live activations under five minutes, and repeat use by at least four of five eligible accounts. Also require aggregate contribution of at least 70%, no tenant with negative contribution, and no unresolved tenant-isolation defect. These are proposed operating thresholds, not industry benchmarks. Apply safety and cost defects as Fix conditions before considering higher acquisition volume.

Everything between Kill and Scale is Fix, with one named constraint, one owner, and a seven-day retest budget. A product with seven paying logos and healthy contribution needs a different intervention from ten logos whose usage loses money. In the first case, test one narrower buyer segment or improve the demonstration; in the second, adjust credits, routing, or price before buying more traffic. If the Scale conditions pass, double only the small measured outreach batch, not payroll or infrastructure commitments. Thirty days cannot establish annual retention, durable acquisition cost, or lifetime value. Continue cohort tracking through renewals and reserve cash for refunds and service costs. If killing the offer, stop new sales, settle pilot commitments, provide promised exports, and preserve only the research records permitted by the agreed retention terms.
